memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'The high priest, the one among his brothers who has had the anointing
oil poured on his head and who has been ordained to wear the priestly
garments, must not let his hair become unkempt or tear his clothes.
He must not enter a place where there is a dead body. He must not make
himself unclean, even for his father or mother'" - Lev 21:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The ordinary priest could mourn for his closest family. The high
priest could not, even for his own father or mother. Why the
difference? Because he alone entered the Most Holy Place. He alone
stood before the ark on the Day of Atonement, representing the entire
nation before God. His role was so weighty that not even personal
grief could interrupt it.

Think about what that meant for him as a human being. This was a costly
calling. Yet it was still only a shadow.

Now look at Jesus. He is our great High Priest, anointed not with oil
but with the Spirit (Acts 10:38). He did not need to avoid death - He
walked straight into it. And unlike Aaron's line, He never needed to
step aside for another. The book of Hebrews says that because He lives
forever, He has a permanent priesthood and can save completely those
who come to God through Him (Heb 7:24-25).

Dear friend, the old high priest could not stop his ministry to grieve.
Our High Priest never stops His ministry at all. Right now He is
interceding for you. Not occasionally. Continuously.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What comfort do I find in knowing Jesus is praying for me right now?
2. Am I coming to God through Christ, or trying to approach Him some
   other way?
3. How does Christ's permanent priesthood steady me in unstable
   seasons?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, thank You that You are my High Priest who never sleeps and
never stops interceding. I come to the Father through You alone today.
Amen.
